description: Compute the potential-determining free-energy step of the oxygen reduction reaction on Pt(111) under the Computational Hydrogen Electrode model.
user_prompt: Compute the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) reaction profile on the Pt(111) FCC surface (space group Fm-3m) via the associative mechanism (O2 -> *OOH -> *O -> *OH -> H2O) under the Computational Hydrogen Electrode (CHE) model. Build the CHE free-energy ladder for the four proton-coupled electron-transfer steps at U = 1.23 V vs RHE and identify the potential-determining step. Report the free energy of the potential-determining PCET step, delta_G_rds = max(delta_G_1..4) (in eV).

references: Norskov, Rossmeisl, Logadottir, Lindqvist, Kitchin, Bligaard & Jonsson, J. Phys. Chem. B 108, 17886 (2004)
Kulkarni, Siahrostami, Patel & Norskov, Chem. Rev. 118, 2302 (2018)
method.modeling: Use a Pt(111) slab with at least 4 layers, vacuum >= 15 Angstrom, and a 2x2x1 or larger surface cell; follow the associative ORR pathway through *OOH, *O, and *OH with triplet O2 as the initial state. Build the CHE free-energy ladder at U = 1.23 V vs RHE and identify delta_G_rds from the four PCET steps.

key_parameters.magnetism: ISPIN=1 for Pt slabs; ISPIN=2 for triplet O2
key_parameters.free_energy_corrections: CHE with ZPE and entropy corrections at 298 K

method.rationale: Norskov et al. report an uphill free-energy step of 0.45 eV for O* reduction to OH* on Pt(111) at U = 1.23 V; this value is used as the reference delta_G_rds. The corresponding limiting potential and theoretical overpotential are derived quantities, U_L = 1.23 V - delta_G_rds/e = 0.78 V and eta = delta_G_rds/e = 0.45 V, while the benchmark scores only delta_G_rds. Kulkarni et al. give a later ORR volcano review value near 0.4 V for Pt(111), and the +/-0.20 eV tolerance covers this literature spread and CHE correction choices.
